title: The Convent on the Pincio: a Lubeck Lutheran, the Guild of Saint Luke, and Fifty-Nine Years of Rome
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Lubeck, birth in the burgomaster's house
stops.date_confidence: attested; English and German Wikipedia agree on 3 July 1789
stops.campa: On the third of July a son is born to Christian Adolph Overbeck, doctor of law, poet, and burgomaster of the free city of Lubeck, in the family house in the Konigstrasse. Behind the father stand three generations of Lutheran pastors and civic officials; the household governs the city and writes its hymns. The boy is given the names Johann Friedrich. He will leave this city at sixteen for Vienna and afterward see it only through canvases sent north by freight, one of which will hang in its largest church for a hundred and eighteen years.
suggested_refs: The Overbeck family house in the Konigstrasse, Lubeck

stops.name: Lubeck, Marienkirche: the assumed baptism
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction [R]: no biographer quotes a baptismal register; the church and the month are inferred from patrician Lubeck custom alone, and the day is defaulted
stops.campa: The great brick church of Saint Mary stands over the Konigstrasse quarter, and by the custom of patrician Lubeck the infants of such houses are carried into it within days of birth. No biographer quotes a baptismal register for this one. The church is entered here on the strength of the custom and nothing else. Thirty-five years on he will send back to these same walls a canvas of Christ entering Jerusalem, and the walls will hold it for a hundred and eighteen years before an incendiary night takes it down.
sources: Reconstruction from Lubeck patrician custom; no primary baptismal record cited in any source consulted
suggested_refs: The Marienkirche of Lubeck, parish church of the Konigstrasse patriciate

stops.name: Lubeck, the Katharineum: the Prima class
stops.date_confidence: attested to September 1803 (German Wikipedia); the day is not recorded and is defaulted to the first
stops.campa: At Michaelmas he enters the Prima class of the Katharineum, the old Latin school lodged in the buildings of a dissolved Franciscan house beside the Katharinenkirche. The curriculum is Latin, Greek, and scripture. That reading list becomes the inventory of his subjects for sixty years: the Gospels read as history, the saints read as fact, Dante and Tasso read as sacred allegory rather than as literature. A Lutheran grammar school hands a future Catholic painter his iconography.
suggested_refs: The Katharineum zu Lubeck in the Konigstrasse, in the former Franciscan monastery

stops.name: Lubeck, Peroux's instruction and the artillery sergeant
stops.date_confidence: year attested for Peroux (German Wikipedia); the Mau lessons are attested but undated; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: His first drawing master is a man named Mau, a non-commissioned officer of artillery who teaches him line the way a gunner knows line. In 1804 he passes to the painter Joseph Nicolaus Peroux for formal instruction. No source records the street of Peroux's workshop; the pin marks the old-town quarter and nothing narrower than that. Two years of it decide him. The burgomaster's son will not read law, and the burgomaster, poet enough himself to understand the case, does not stand in the way.
suggested_refs: Joseph Nicolaus Peroux, Lubeck painter and Overbeck's first formal master

stops.name: Lubeck, the Holstentor: departure for Vienna
stops.date_confidence: date attested by German Wikipedia (6 March); English Wikipedia gives only March 1806. The gate itself is reconstruction [R]
stops.campa: On the sixth of March he leaves for Vienna and the Academy of Fine Arts. He is sixteen. He does not live in Lubeck again, and no source records him setting foot in the city after this day, though canvases of his will travel north for the rest of the century and one will hang in the Marienkirche for four generations. Which gate he used is nowhere written down. The Holstentor stands here for the western road out, the road every traveler south from Lubeck took. The canvas he will one day carry over the Alps is not yet begun.
suggested_refs: The Holstentor, western gate of Lubeck

segments.name: Vienna, and the Guild of Saint Luke

stops.name: Vienna, the St.-Anna-Hof: the Academy under Fuger
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the month of enrollment is not recorded. He left Lubeck on 6 March 1806, so a spring arrival is inferred [R]
stops.campa: The Academy in these years is not the Schillerplatz palace of the later century, which is built only in the 1870s and occupied in 1877; it sits in the St.-Anna-Hof in the Annagasse, inside the walls. Here Heinrich Friedrich Fuger teaches history painting in the approved manner: antique statuary, correct contour, the smooth finish of the age. Overbeck copies antique casts for two years and keeps his objection to himself. Nothing in Fuger's programme touches the painting he means to make, and the programme is the only one Vienna offers.
suggested_refs: The St.-Anna-Hof, Annagasse 3, seat of the Vienna Academy before 1877

stops.name: Vienna, the letter to his father
stops.date_confidence: year attested (English Wikipedia); month and day not recorded and defaulted
stops.campa: In 1808 he writes home that the teaching has neither heart, nor soul, nor sensation in it. He is nineteen and has decided the fault is not his own. His remedy is a book rather than a method: he will take scripture itself for the ground he stands on, and paint out of it. Fuger's studio is full of Greeks; the student's imagination is full of Nazareth. Five other students in the same rooms reach the same conclusion in the same season, and within a year they have a name and a rule for it.
stops.quote: I will abide by the Bible; I elect it as my standing-point.
stops.quote_source: J. Beavington Atkinson, Overbeck (Sampson Low, London, 1882), p. 18, on his resolve during the Vienna Academy years
sources: J. Beavington Atkinson, Overbeck (Sampson Low, 1882), p. 18, via archive.org identifiers overbeck00atkiiala and overbeck01atkigoog
suggested_refs: Overbeck's Vienna letters to his father, quoted in Atkinson (1882) and in Howitt (1886)

stops.name: Vienna, the founding of the Lukasbund
stops.date_confidence: year attested (German and English Wikipedia); no month given in any source consulted, so month and day are defaulted
stops.campa: Six students bind themselves into a brotherhood named for Luke, patron of painters and, by tradition, the first man to paint the Virgin from life: Overbeck, Franz Pforr, Ludwig Vogel, Johann Konrad Hottinger, Joseph Wintergerst, Joseph Sutter. They take a medieval guild for their model inside an academy built to abolish guilds. Their program is Durer and Perugino against the late Raphael, honest severe outline against the washed-out manner of the day, and religion as the proper subject of painting rather than one subject among many.
stops.quote: Oh, I was so full of it, my whole fancy was possessed by Madonnas and Christs.
stops.quote_source: J. Beavington Atkinson, Overbeck (Sampson Low, London, 1882), p. 18, Overbeck on his longing for Christian subject matter
suggested_refs: The statutes and membership of the Lukasbund, Vienna 1809

stops.name: Vienna, expelled, and the road opened
stops.date_confidence: expulsion attested to 1810; the Allgemeine Deutsche Biographie gives travel south in spring 1810 and arrival in Rome on 20 June, so an April departure is inferred [R]
stops.campa: After roughly four years of open conflict the Academy, reorganizing itself after 1809, does not readmit them; it expels them. Overbeck rolls up a half-finished canvas of Christ's Entry into Jerusalem, joins Pforr and Vogel, and turns south in the spring. He is twenty, without a diploma and without a patron, and he enters no other school. The brotherhood the Academy has just broken up holds together in Rome for two more years. Its founder stays there fifty-nine.
stops.quote: What has been our crime? It is in great measure that we have striven after a severe outline, in opposition to the loose, cloudy, washed-out manner of the day.
stops.quote_source: J. Beavington Atkinson, Overbeck (Sampson Low, London, 1882), p. 25, Overbeck defending the Lukasbund against academic critics
suggested_refs: The 1809-1810 reorganization of the Vienna Academy, under which the Lukasbund students were excluded

stops.name: Brenner Pass, the crossing that is not documented
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction [R]: no itinerary of the 1810 journey survives in any source reached. The pass, month and day are all inferred from the standard route
stops.campa: The route from Vienna to Rome in the spring of 1810 is nowhere itemized. No letter, no diary, no itinerary survives in anything reachable. The Brenner is the crossing German travelers to Italy use in this century, and it is entered here as a reconstruction and not as a fact. What is fixed is the two ends: they leave Vienna in the spring and stand inside Rome on the twentieth of June. Between those points the map is honest guesswork, and the canvas of the Entry into Jerusalem is somewhere in the baggage.
sources: Reconstruction from standard early-19th-century Vienna to Rome travel; no primary itinerary located
suggested_refs: The Brenner post road, principal Alpine crossing for German travelers to Italy

stops.name: Venice, Piazza San Marco: a gap left open
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction [R], unattested: no source names Venice as a stop on the 1810 journey
stops.campa: Venice is not named as a stop by any source consulted. It is placed here because it is the first Italian city on the standard road down from the Alps, and because a party of young painters who have just staked their lives on Perugino and the age before Raphael would not have passed the Bellinis without looking. That is an argument from character and not a document, and it should fall the moment a letter turns up saying otherwise. The pin is recorded as a gap so that no later researcher mistakes it for evidence.
sources: Reconstruction, unattested; recorded as a gap in the itinerary
suggested_refs: The Bellini altarpieces of Venice, the northern Italian quattrocento the Lukasbund had made its model

stops.name: Florence, Piazza della Signoria: the same hunger, a generation early
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction [R], unattested: no source names Florence as a stop; the date is a placeholder between the Alps and the attested Rome arrival of 20 June
stops.campa: Florence appears in no source as a station of the 1810 journey. The Grand Tour road runs through it and every northern artist of the period stops, so the logic is strong and the evidence is absent; the pin is a reconstruction and nothing more. Two generations later Edward Burne-Jones comes to this square hunting Botticelli and Fra Angelico for exactly the quality the Lukasbund crossed the Alps to find, and William Morris turns to the Middle Ages in England for the same reason. Nobody can say whether Overbeck saw the same panels going south.
sources: Reconstruction, unattested; recorded as a gap
suggested_refs: The Uffizi and San Marco panels that drew both the Nazarenes and, fifty years later, the Pre-Raphaelites

segments.name: Rome: the Convent and the Baptism

stops.name: Rome, the Porta del Popolo: entry
stops.date_confidence: day attested by the Allgemeine Deutsche Biographie; Wikipedia gives only the year 1810. The gate is reconstruction [R]
stops.campa: On the twentieth of June they enter Rome. Northern travelers come in through the Porta del Popolo, off the Flaminian road, into the piazza where three streets open like a fan; the sources give the day and the fact of arrival but not the gate, and the gate is inference. He is twenty and expelled from an academy. He has fifty-nine years left and will spend every one of them inside this city. The canvas of Christ entering Jerusalem, begun in Vienna, comes in with him unfinished and stays unfinished for fourteen years.
suggested_refs: The Porta del Popolo, northern gate of Rome and standard entry of German travelers

stops.name: Rome, the quarter below the Trinita dei Monti
stops.date_confidence: the quarter is attested as the northern painters' district; no address for Overbeck is recorded, and the pin is inherited unchanged from the corpus rather than derived [R]
stops.campa: The quarter under the Trinita dei Monti is where every foreign painter in Rome keeps a room and a model, and has been for decades before he arrives. Johann Heinrich Wilhelm Tischbein took his lodging in these streets in 1779 on a Kassel stipend, and no letter names his door either; the pin here is Tischbein's, inherited without alteration. The Germans in Rome are a village inside a city, passing addresses, models and stipends along by word of mouth. Overbeck enters that village at twenty and keeps a room in it until he dies.
suggested_refs: The Piazza di Spagna and Trinita dei Monti quarter, lodging district of the northern artists in Rome

stops.name: Rome, the convent of Sant'Isidoro a Capo le Case
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the month of the move into the convent is not recorded and is defaulted. The commonly repeated roster of the community is anachronistic for 1810, see campa
stops.campa: Four of them take rooms in the half-abandoned Franciscan convent of Sant'Isidoro on the Pincian slope: Overbeck, Pforr, Vogel, Hottinger. They live under something like a rule, praying, fasting and drawing, each man in his own cell. Rome names them i Nazareni for the long hair worn alla nazarena. Peter von Cornelius and Wilhelm von Schadow reach the city only in 1811 and Philipp Veit not until 1815, so the famous roster of the convent is a composite of years the common life itself did not survive; it has broken up by 1812.
suggested_refs: The convent of Sant'Isidoro a Capo le Case, Via degli Artisti 41, Rome

stops.name: Rome, Via del Corso: the house Goethe kept
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction [R]: no source places Overbeck at this address. The pin is inherited byte-identical from the corpus and marks a ground, not an event; the date is a placeholder
stops.campa: A quarter of an hour's walk from Sant'Isidoro stands the house on the Corso where Johann Wolfgang von Goethe lodged with Tischbein from October 1786 and counted his entry into Rome a second birth. Goethe came to Rome to be cured of the north by antiquity. Overbeck comes to be cured of antiquity by the north's own older faith, and arrives twenty-four years later on the same axis of streets. No source puts Overbeck at this door. The pin is inherited from the corpus and marks a ground, not a meeting.
suggested_refs: The Casa di Goethe, Via del Corso 18, Rome

stops.name: Rome, the first commission
stops.date_confidence: attested: two letters of 16 and 20 December 1811 quoted verbatim by Atkinson (1882), p. 29. The commission is Queen Caroline of Bavaria's, not the Casa Bartholdy, which comes five years later
stops.campa: The struggling painter's first order comes not from a Roman patron but from Queen Caroline of Bavaria, who wants an Adoration of the Kings in oils. He writes on the sixteenth of December that he was so overpowered with joy he could not bring out a syllable, and asks what can be the cause of his good fortune. Four days later he writes home to Lubeck. He is twenty-two. It is the first money his art has made and the first proof that the road out of Vienna went somewhere other than into the ditch.
stops.quote: Henceforth and for ever I am a man and an independent artist in the workshop, free as a king over the boundless domain of fantasy to create a beautiful world.
stops.quote_source: J. Beavington Atkinson, Overbeck (Sampson Low, London, 1882), p. 29, Overbeck's letter to Lubeck of 20 December 1811
sources: Atkinson, Overbeck (1882), pp. 28-29, via archive.org overbeck00atkiiala and overbeck01atkigoog
suggested_refs: Overbeck's Adoration of the Kings, painted for Queen Caroline of Bavaria

stops.name: Rome, the conversion
stops.date_confidence: sources disagree and are not reconciled here: German Wikipedia gives April 1813; Atkinson (1882) gives Whitsuntide 1813, which fell on 6 June. The year is firm, the month is not
stops.campa: He is received into the Roman Catholic Church, the decisive break with three generations of Lubeck Lutherans. His confessor is Professor Pietro Ostini, afterward cardinal; the poet Zacharias Werner stands godfather. German record puts it in April, Atkinson at Whitsuntide, which fell on the sixth of June; the year is firm and the month is not. The painting has been Christian in subject for four years and is now Christian in obedience. Some of the brotherhood follow him across and others do not.
stops.quote: Overbeck at Whitsuntide in the year 1813 joined the Catholic Faith, and with joy entered into the family of the world's Church.
stops.quote_source: J. Beavington Atkinson, Overbeck (Sampson Low, London, 1882), pp. 33-34, quoting the record of the conversion
suggested_refs: Cardinal Pietro Ostini, Overbeck's confessor; Zacharias Werner, his godfather at the conversion

segments.name: The Walls: Bartholdy, Massimo, and the Roman Household

stops.name: Rome, Palazzo Zuccari: the Casa Bartholdy frescoes
stops.date_confidence: sources disagree and are not reconciled: German Wikipedia dates the Joseph cycle to 1816/17, English Wikipedia to 1818. The earliest year in the range is used and the month defaulted
stops.campa: Jakob Salomon Bartholdy, Prussian consul-general and himself a convert, rents rooms in the Palazzo Zuccari on the Via Gregoriana and gives four Germans a wall apiece. Overbeck paints Joseph sold by his brethren and the seven years of famine; Cornelius, Veit and Schadow take the rest of the story. It is called the first revival of buon fresco of the century. The frescoes are later cut out of the walls and carried to Berlin, where the Joseph cycle hangs in the Alte Nationalgalerie.
stops.quote: Overbeck from Lübeck is the one who by the gentleness and nobility of his soul draws all around him; he inspires them to everything true and beautiful.
stops.quote_source: Peter von Cornelius on Overbeck, quoted in J. Beavington Atkinson, Overbeck (Sampson Low, London, 1882), p. 20
suggested_refs: The Casa Bartholdy frescoes, Palazzo Zuccari, Via Gregoriana 28, now in the Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin

stops.name: Rome, the Casino Massimo Lancellotti: the Tasso room
stops.date_confidence: the campaign runs 1817-1828 per German Wikipedia; English Wikipedia dates the commission to 1818. The opening year is used and the month defaulted
stops.campa: Prince Massimo gives the brotherhood a garden pavilion on the Via Matteo Boiardo near the Lateran and divides three Italian poets among them: Veit and Koch take Dante, Schnorr von Carolsfeld takes Ariosto, Overbeck takes Tasso. He works at the Tasso room across more than a decade and does not finish it. Joseph von Fuhrich completes it between 1819 and 1827; the Italian record names both men, and the room passes into the guidebooks as Overbeck's alone.
suggested_refs: The Casino Massimo Lancellotti, Via Matteo Boiardo 16, Rome: Dante, Ariosto and Tasso rooms

stops.name: Rome, the marriage to Nina Hartl
stops.date_confidence: the Allgemeine Deutsche Biographie gives autumn 1818; the day is not recorded and is defaulted. German Wikipedia names the wife only as Anna, born about 1790
stops.campa: In the autumn of 1818 he marries Nina Hartl, whom his German biographer calls the beautiful Viennese; the German encyclopedia gives her name as Anna and her birth as about 1790. A son, Alfons Maria, is born about the following year, and two daughters die in infancy. The domestic record is thin: names without dates, dates without names, one clause in a German encyclopedia's family paragraph standing in for a marriage of thirty-five years. She dies in Rome in 1853 and he outlives her by sixteen years.
suggested_refs: The Overbeck family record: Nina (Anna) Hartl, the son Alfons Maria, and the two daughters dead in infancy

stops.name: Lubeck, Marienkirche: the Entry into Jerusalem installed
stops.date_confidence: year attested (English and German Wikipedia); month and day not recorded and defaulted. No source records Overbeck traveling with the picture or returning to Lubeck
stops.campa: The canvas he carried out of Vienna half-finished in 1810 is completed in Rome fourteen years later and sent north to the church of his baptism. He does not travel with it. A Catholic convert in Rome hangs a Christ over a Lutheran congregation in the city he left at sixteen, and the entire transaction is conducted by freight. The painting hangs there until the night of the twenty-ninth of March 1942. Another Overbeck, a Lamentation of Christ, survives in the prayer chapel of the north ambulatory to this day.
suggested_refs: Christ's Entry into Jerusalem (1824), Marienkirche Lubeck, destroyed 1942

stops.name: Rome, Munich and Dusseldorf refused
stops.date_confidence: year attested for both offers (German Wikipedia); no month given in either case and both are defaulted
stops.campa: Munich offers him a professorship and he declines it. Dusseldorf offers in the same year and he declines that too. Peter von Cornelius, who came to Sant'Isidoro in 1811, will run Munich; Wilhelm von Schadow, who came the same year, will run Dusseldorf. The brotherhood is becoming the German art establishment and its founder is not going with it. He stays in a Roman studio, sixteen years into a residence with thirty-nine years still to run, and lets the others carry the movement home.
stops.quote: No one who saw or heard him speak could question his purity of motive, his deep insight and abounding knowledge: he is a treasury of art and poetry and a saintly man.
stops.quote_source: Wilhelm von Schadow on Overbeck, quoted in J. Beavington Atkinson, Overbeck (Sampson Low, London, 1882), p. 24
suggested_refs: The Munich and Dusseldorf academies under Cornelius and Schadow, the Nazarene movement institutionalized

stops.name: Rome, Italia und Germania
stops.date_confidence: year attested (English and German Wikipedia); month and day not recorded and defaulted
stops.campa: He paints two women seated and holding hands, one dark and laurel-crowned against an Italian hill town, one fair and myrtle-crowned against German gables. It is the doctrine of the brotherhood reduced to a single canvas: the Italian quattrocento and the German late Gothic are not rivals but sisters, and the modern German painter's business is to marry them. Franz Pforr, who founded the Lukasbund with him in Vienna and died at twenty-four in 1812, has been in the ground sixteen years and does not see it.
suggested_refs: Italia und Germania (1828), Neue Pinakothek, Munich

stops.name: Rome, the Frankfurt directorship refused
stops.date_confidence: year attested (German Wikipedia); month and day not recorded and defaulted
stops.campa: The Stadelsches Kunstinstitut at Frankfurt offers him its directorship and he refuses it, the third German institution in four years to be told no. Munich went to Cornelius, Dusseldorf to Schadow; the brotherhood's founders take the chairs and its founder stays where he is. He is forty and has been in Rome nineteen years. Eleven years later the Stadel will get the largest programmatic canvas of his life instead of his person, which is the arrangement he has been offering Germany since he left it.
suggested_refs: The Stadelsches Kunstinstitut, Frankfurt am Main, and its 1829 offer to Overbeck

stops.name: Spoleto, the road north that is not documented
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction [R]: no source describes how, or whether, Overbeck traveled to Assisi for the Porziuncola commission. Place, month and day are all inferred from the Via Flaminia route
stops.campa: The road from Rome to Assisi is the old Via Flaminia and every traveler between the two cities uses it. Spoleto sits on that road, and Spoleto is entered here as a waypoint reconstructed from the geography rather than from any itinerary of his. No source consulted describes how he went north for the Porziuncola commission, or whether he went at all rather than sending cartoons to be executed. The pin is the road and not the man. This is the only journey outside Rome the sources oblige him to have made in fifty-nine years.
sources: Reconstruction from the standard Rome to Assisi road; unattested
suggested_refs: The Via Flaminia between Rome and Assisi

stops.name: Assisi, the Porziuncola: the Vision of Saint Francis
stops.date_confidence: sources disagree and are not reconciled: German Wikipedia and the English Portiuncula article give 1829, the English Overbeck article gives 1830. Month defaulted. The often-repeated figure of 6.5 metres is unsupported by any source consulted
stops.campa: Inside the great basilica of Santa Maria degli Angeli, down on the plain below Assisi, stands the small stone chapel where Francis lived and died, swallowed whole by the church built to protect it. Over its outer door Overbeck paints Francis receiving the indulgence from Christ and the Virgin, beneath the legend Haec est porta vitae aeternae. It is called his largest fresco. The convent that housed him in Rome at twenty-one was Franciscan and half empty; the chapel he paints over here is where the order began.
suggested_refs: The Porziuncola fresco, Basilica di Santa Maria degli Angeli, Assisi

stops.name: Rome, the death of his son
stops.date_confidence: year attested (German Wikipedia); no month, day, age or cause is given in any source consulted, and the identification with Alfons Maria is inference [R]
stops.campa: His son dies in Rome. The sources give the year and nothing else: no age, no illness, no rite, one clause in a German encyclopedia's family paragraph. The boy is presumably the Alfons Maria born about 1819, which would make him twenty-one, but no source states it. Two daughters have already died in infancy. In the same year the largest canvas of his life is finished and crated for Frankfurt, and the two facts sit side by side in the record with nothing at all joining them.
suggested_refs: The Overbeck family graves in the Campo Santo Teutonico, Vatican City

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, the Stadel: The Triumph of Religion in the Arts
stops.date_confidence: year attested (English and German Wikipedia); month and day not recorded and defaulted. No source records Overbeck traveling with the picture
stops.campa: The canvas arrives at the Stadelsches Kunstinstitut eleven years after he refused to direct it. It is a summa: every art laid at the feet of religion, painters and poets and musicians ranked in tiers beneath a Virgin, the argument of the Lukasbund enlarged into an altarpiece for a museum. He writes his own explanatory text for the picture, and in that text he settles the account with antiquity that the Vienna Academy could never get out of him. There is no record that he traveled with it.
stops.quote: Although heathenism, as such, should be looked upon by the Christian painter with decided disdain, yet the arts as well as the literature of the ancients may be turned to advantage, as the children of Israel employed the gold and silver vessels which they brought with them out of Egypt in the service of the true God in His Temple, after melting them down and consecrating them anew.
stops.quote_source: Overbeck's explanatory text to The Triumph of Religion in the Arts, quoted in J. Beavington Atkinson, Overbeck (Sampson Low, London, 1882), p. 14
suggested_refs: Der Triumph der Religion in den Kunsten (1840), Stadel Museum, Schaumainkai 63, Frankfurt

stops.name: Rome, the papal commission: Christ Fleeing Persecution
stops.date_confidence: German Wikipedia gives the campaign as 1848-1857; months not recorded and defaulted. The Papal Gold Medal of Merit is attested to 1850
stops.campa: He begins Christ Fleeing Persecution on a papal commission and works at it for nearly a decade, finishing in 1857. In 1850 he is given the Papal Gold Medal of Merit. He is fifty-nine when he starts and past sixty-eight when he stops. His patron is a Church rather than a market, and the work takes as long as it takes. Barthold Georg Niebuhr had called him incapable by nature of standing alone; he has been in Rome thirty-eight years and painting the same subject throughout.
stops.quote: Overbeck is an enthusiast and quite illiberal; he is a very amiable man and endowed with a magnificent imagination, but incapable by nature of standing alone.
stops.quote_source: Barthold Georg Niebuhr on Overbeck, quoted in J. Beavington Atkinson, Overbeck (Sampson Low, London, 1882), p. 32
suggested_refs: Christus flieht vor der Verfolgung (1848-1857), painted on papal commission

stops.name: Vatican City, Campo Santo Teutonico: the household divided
stops.date_confidence: the death year 1853 is attested (German Wikipedia, which gives the wife as Anna, about 1790 to 1853); month and day not recorded and defaulted
stops.campa: His wife dies in Rome after thirty-five years of marriage. The German record gives the year and nothing else, no month, no day, no cause. She is buried, with the son dead in 1840 and the two daughters dead in infancy, in the Campo Santo Teutonico, the German burial ground inside the Vatican walls where Germans in Rome have been laid since the Middle Ages. He will not be buried there with them. Sixteen years later he is laid in a church on the other side of the city, and no source consulted explains the separation.
suggested_refs: The Campo Santo Teutonico, German cemetery within the Vatican walls

stops.name: Rome, the orders of Europe
stops.date_confidence: individual years attested (German Wikipedia): Saint Michael 1839, Maximilian Order 1854, Pour le Merite 1855. Grouped at the last of them; no place of conferral is recorded for any
stops.campa: Bavaria makes him a knight of the Order of Saint Michael in 1839 and of the Maximilian Order in 1854; Prussia gives him the Pour le Merite for arts and sciences in 1855; the Pope has already given him a gold medal. The Protestant states of Germany decorate a Catholic convert who refused all three of their academies, and decorate him because he is the most famous German painter alive. He collects the ribbons in Rome and travels to receive none of them.
suggested_refs: The Bavarian Order of Saint Michael, the Maximilian Order, and the Prussian Pour le Merite for arts and sciences

stops.name: Cologne Cathedral, the Assumption of the Madonna
stops.date_confidence: sources disagree and are not reconciled: English Wikipedia gives 1855, German Wikipedia gives 1857. The earlier is used for ordering only; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: He paints an Assumption of the Madonna for the cathedral at Cologne, unfinished for six hundred years and now being completed by a Prussian state that has decided the Gothic is German. The picture goes north like all the others, by freight, out of a studio in Rome. English record dates the work to 1855 and German record to 1857, and no source reached adjudicates between them; both years stand here rather than one being quietly chosen. The pin is the destination, not the easel.
suggested_refs: The Assumption of the Madonna, Cologne Cathedral

stops.name: Rome, Pius IX at the painter's door
stops.date_confidence: the 1858 commission is attested (English Wikipedia); the papal visit to Overbeck's house is attested but undated in German Wikipedia, and is anchored here to the commission year for ordering only [R]
stops.campa: Pius IX commissions from him a tempera of Christ delivered to the Jews in 1858, part of the same Passion sequence as the Christ Fleeing Persecution. At some point the Pope comes in person to the painter's house in Rome, a visit no source dates. A Lubeck Lutheran's son, expelled from an imperial academy at twenty-one, is called on at home by the Pope in his own workshop. The address is not recorded either; the pin is the quarter below the Pincio where the northern painters have always lodged.
suggested_refs: Christus wird den Juden ausgeliefert, commissioned by Pius IX, 1858

stops.name: Munich, Neue Pinakothek: Die Taufe
stops.date_confidence: English Wikipedia gives a range of 1862 to 1864; the opening year is used and the month defaulted. The pin is the picture's present home, not the studio where it was made
stops.campa: He paints a Baptism, which will hang in the Neue Pinakothek at Munich, the city whose professorship he turned down thirty-six years earlier and whose academy Cornelius went on to direct. English record gives the work a range of 1862 to 1864 and no narrower. He is seventy-three. The subject is the one his whole life turned on, and he has been painting it, in one form or another, since he came into the Church at twenty-three. He does not go to Munich to see it hung.
suggested_refs: Die Taufe, Neue Pinakothek, Munich

stops.name: Boston, elected in absentia
stops.date_confidence: year attested (English Wikipedia); month and day not recorded and defaulted. The pin marks the electing institution's city, not a place Overbeck stood; he never crossed the Atlantic [R]
stops.campa: The American Academy of Arts and Sciences elects him a Foreign Honorary Member. He has never crossed the Atlantic and will not; the pin marks the institution's city and not a place he stood. Fifty-five years after six students were put out of the Vienna Academy, a learned society in Massachusetts enters a Roman convert on its rolls beside its natural philosophers. He is seventy-five and has five years to live, and he has not left Italy since 1810.
suggested_refs: The rolls of Foreign Honorary Members, American Academy of Arts and Sciences, 1864

stops.name: Rome, death in the painters' quarter
stops.date_confidence: attested (English and German Wikipedia); the street address of the house is not recorded in any source consulted, and the pin is the quarter
stops.campa: He dies in Rome on the twelfth of November, eighty years old. Fifty-nine of those years have been spent inside this city; Lubeck had him for sixteen and Vienna for four. The brotherhood he founded lasted two years in its convent, and Franz Pforr, who swore to it with him, has been dead fifty-seven. He came in through a gate in June 1810 with a rolled canvas and an expulsion. He goes out of a house in the painters' quarter whose street nobody troubled to write down.
suggested_refs: The northern painters' quarter below the Pincio, where Overbeck died

stops.name: Rome, San Bernardo alle Terme: the burial
stops.date_confidence: burial in the chapel of St Francis attested (English and German Wikipedia); the exact day is not recorded and is defaulted. The date of Hoffmann's epitaph is unsourced
stops.campa: He is buried in the chapel of Saint Francis inside San Bernardo alle Terme on the Via Torino, a round church made out of a corner tower of the Baths of Diocletian: a Christian tomb inside a repurposed pagan monument, which is the argument of his whole career reduced to masonry. Karl Hoffmann, sculptor, his confirmation godchild and his son-in-law both, carves the epitaph. The claim that he worshipped in this church regularly is repeated in some accounts and supported by none consulted.
suggested_refs: The chapel of St Francis, San Bernardo alle Terme, Via Torino 94, Rome, with Karl Hoffmann's epitaph

stops.name: Penymynydd, Overbeck murals in a Welsh parish church
stops.date_confidence: the 1843 build date and Troughton's twenty years of painting are attested (English Wikipedia); the murals themselves span roughly 1843 to 1863 and no single year fits them
stops.campa: The Glynne family of Hawarden build a church at Penymynydd in Flintshire in 1843. Its first vicar, the Reverend John Ellis Troughton, spends the first twenty years of the building's life painting its interior with Overbeck murals. Overbeck is alive, in Rome, and has in all likelihood never heard of the place. The Nazarene manner has become a pattern book by now, an iconography reproducible by a country clergyman with a brush and a print, a long way from six students swearing themselves to Luke in Vienna.
suggested_refs: The Church of St John the Baptist, Penymynydd, Flintshire, and its Troughton murals

stops.name: Freiburg im Breisgau, Margaret Howitt's biography
stops.date_confidence: publication attested to 1886 with the Freiburg Herder imprint (English Wikipedia bibliography); the widely repeated claim that Howitt was Overbeck's amanuensis in Rome is unsupported by any source reached and is left standing as tradition only [R]
stops.campa: Margaret Howitt, English writer and daughter of William and Mary Howitt, publishes Friedrich Overbeck: sein Leben und sein Schaffen in two volumes with Herder at Freiburg, working from the painter's papers with his family's cooperation. It becomes the standing German biography and the ground of most later Nazarene scholarship. A widespread tradition makes her Overbeck's amanuensis in Rome in his last years. No source reached supports it, and the tradition is separated here from the book and left standing on its own.
sources: Margaret Howitt, Friedrich Overbeck: sein Leben und sein Schaffen, 2 vols (Freiburg im Breisgau: Herder, 1886)
suggested_refs: Howitt's two-volume Overbeck (Herder, 1886), the standing German biography

stops.name: Lubeck, the Behnhaus: the estate comes home
stops.date_confidence: the 1914 donation by Charlotte Overbeck and the Behnhaus Nazarene collection are attested (German Wikipedia); the retrospective years 1977, 1981, 1984 and 1989 are attested separately and named in the campa
stops.campa: Charlotte Overbeck gives the artist's estate to the city in 1914, and the Behnhaus in the Konigstrasse builds a Nazarene collection around him and his circle. A century after his death the retrospectives come: Frankfurt in 1977, Rome in 1981, Munich in 1984, Lubeck in 1989. The city he left at sixteen and never re-entered holds the papers and the paintings and becomes the center of his modern rediscovery, while Rome keeps the frescoes and the grave.
suggested_refs: The Behnhaus, Konigstrasse 9/11, Lubeck: Nazarene collection from the 1914 Overbeck bequest

stops.name: Lubeck, the Overbeck-Gesellschaft
stops.date_confidence: founding year attested (German Wikipedia); month and day not recorded and defaulted
stops.campa: In the last year of the war Lubeck founds an art society and names it for the Nazarene born in its Konigstrasse and for his family, forty-nine years after his death in Rome. Its exhibition building stands in the Burgergarten behind the Behnhaus. The society is not a memorial: it shows contemporary work from the start and goes on showing it into the twenty-first century. His name stands over a hall of the modern painting he argued against for fifty years, in the city he did not return to.
suggested_refs: The Overbeck-Gesellschaft exhibition building, Burgergarten, Lubeck

stops.name: Lubeck, Marienkirche: Palm Sunday, 1942
stops.date_confidence: attested; German Wikipedia dates the raid precisely to 29 March 1942, English record gives Palm Sunday 1942. The absence of any replacement is an argument from silence [R]
stops.campa: On the night of the twenty-ninth of March, Palm Sunday, Allied incendiaries burn out the interior of the Marienkirche. Christ's Entry into Jerusalem, begun in Vienna in 1810 and hung here in 1824, burns with it. No copy, reconstruction or replacement is recorded, though that is an argument from silence and is entered as one. The picture that opened his working life and closed the circle back to his baptismal church is gone. A Lamentation of Christ by him survives in the prayer chapel of the north ambulatory.
suggested_refs: The Palm Sunday raid on Lubeck, 29 March 1942, and the losses in the Marienkirche
